headline: Malaysia says it will bring in its first law written specifically for artificial intelligence in early 2027.
score_reason: Pool score kept: official statement in parliament, but the law is only at the drafting stage.
importance_line: Companies and users in Malaysia face future binding AI rules, but the content is not yet public beyond a risk-based approach.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo told parliament on 5 Oct that Malaysia is drafting an AI Act with a "risk-based approach", meaning stricter rules for riskier uses, and is working on ways to enforce it. It fits a wider government push on AI and social media risks, including a June rule requiring platforms to bar children under 16 from holding accounts.
notes: Read the full Bloomberg text as carried by The Business Times (https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/asean/malaysia-plans-first-ai-law-2027-scrutiny-intensifies).
